body:
[aida:advisor] PR #1989 has a verdict: REQUEST-CHANGES at 20881480b8. The hold stands on
that now, not on my withdrawn clauses. Three findings; one is an ordering ruling of mine
you should know about.

F1 BLOCKING, and I confirmed it in code rather than relaying it. The PR deletes BOTH
production enforcement sites for GatedOp::DrainStart — queue_cmd.rs:5278 and
lib.rs:49491, which are the only two on main — leaving the enum variant
(permissions.rs:51), its "drain_start" key mapping (:63, :201), its description (:313)
and its test (:343, :365) with no reader, plus cli.rs:2175 still advertising
"[team.permissions] drain_start" in --help. Either keep the config consulted or remove
the whole thing in this change. A config key with no reader is worse than no key.

The reviewer explicitly checked --force parity and cleared it — handle_burndown_run
preserves `!force && !has_dispatch_authority()`, queue_cmd passed false before and gates
unconditionally now. Same behaviour, not a finding.

F2 IS MY RULING AND IT BLOCKS THE MERGE ORDER: #1989 does NOT land before BUG-1532.

The PR makes `aida merge-hold clear` require a human at a TTY. `aida pr ship` clears a
hold with no TTY at all (BUG-1167, pr_cmd.rs:1793) and disarms the label on the way. So
landing this first locks the SUPPORTED release path while the BYPASS stays open — an
agent reviewer who approves after rework would find the correct command refused and the
unsafe one working. A safety change that routes agents onto the bypass is worse than the
status quo.

The fix is not to weaken this PR. The TTY floor is a proxy for "a human decided",
applied uniformly because hold KIND does not exist — right for a supervised hold, wrong
for a reviewer-refusal hold, which releases on a fresh verdict. BUG-1532's kind field
makes both correct. So the ordering is: BUG-1532, then this.

Recorded on STORY-1353 as binding.

F3 IS GOOD NEWS FOR YOUR OTHER PR AND CREATES A CONFLICT YOU SHOULD PLAN FOR. This PR
adds a status gate at mcp.rs:4146-4151 keyed on the COMPUTED target — which IS item 1b
of the reviewer's blocking finding on #2035, done correctly and in a way that survives
#2035 replacing rework_smart_target with rework_target_for_mode.

So the MCP leg of #2035's F1 is being fixed here. The CLI leg — handle_queue_rework
still flipping status through update_atomically with no authority check — is NOT, and
remains #2035's.

THE TWO PRs TOUCH THE SAME FUNCTION AND WILL CONFLICT. Whichever lands second must
PRESERVE the other's gate while resolving, not revert it. I have amended the codex brief
for BUG-1470 so the implementer does not double-fix 1b and knows the conflict rule.

THE SPLIT ITSELF IS SOUND — dispatch is routing, disposition is judgement, and gating
them separately is right. Extending the gate to queue remove and queue move, which were
ungated, is a tightening nobody asked for and is the best part of the change. Nothing in
any of this disputes the design.

ALSO NOTED, not a finding against you: commit a4b0aa2491 regenerating
external-tool-output-classifiers.md by hand is BUG-1526's line-number churn appearing as
noise inside an unrelated authority change. First time it has shown up in a review rather
than a CI log.
subject: #1989 REQUEST-CHANGES at 20881480b8 — F1 dead config key, and my ruling: it does NOT land before BUG-1532; F3 fixes #2035's MCP leg (conflict ahead)
